correctness.rationale: The Weyl overlap produces the stated Hermitian matrix up to conjugation/rephasing. Symbolic expansion gives (1), and the hyperbolic form is strictly positive for positive sides because sinh A sinh B > AB >= sin²(sqrt(AB)). At fixed area the determinant tends to zero at both unbounded eccentricity ends, so a maximum is attained. For sorted sides at vanishing area, a subsequence with long side tending to zero gives zero normalized limit by (8), and one tending to infinity gives the bound π²/a⁴; a positive finite long-side limit gives π⁴F(πa²). A fixed-long-side test produces a positive limit and excludes the first two regimes for maximizing sequences. Q^(5) is strictly negative (e^(2y) >= 1+2y); Q and its first three derivatives start at zero and its fourth starts positive. Each of these functions tends to minus infinity and applying the single sign-change argument successively gives the unique positive root. This pins down every sorted maximizer. Square expansion gives π⁶h⁶/3. The independent symbolic and numerical check reproduces the determinant, derivatives, square coefficient and quoted decimal constants.
residual_risks: No claim about arbitrary placements, other windows, frame bounds, least eigenvalues, or global area dependence.
